what: JFrog runs the warehouse for software. Its Artifactory product stores the compiled packages and container images a company's code depends on, and its security tools scan them for known vulnerabilities.
customers: Software engineering teams at large companies, paid for by subscription per deployment.
money: software run on the customer's own servers
the same platform run by JFrog
moat: Build pipelines point at Artifactory, so moving it means touching every build in the company. Few pieces of developer infrastructure are harder to replace.
risks: 21 times sales for a company still posting a small accounting loss
Developer tool budgets are cut when engineering headcount is cut
GitHub and GitLab bundle package registries into tools customers already pay for
opportunities: $207M of free cash flow and $704M of cash against $13M of debt
Revenue grew from $207M to $532M in four years, and the cloud half grows faster than the whole
Security scanning sells into the same customers at a higher price per seat
watch: Cloud revenue growth and net dollar retention.
